items.text: Backup code comparison via indexOf is case-sensitive. If codes contain letters, users who type them in the wrong case will be rejected. Normalize both sides to the same case before comparing.

Race condition: the backup code read, validation, and invalidation are not atomic. Two concurrent requests can both validate and consume the same backup code, because the findUnique and update are separate queries with no transaction or lock.
Component exported from BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor instead of BackupCode, making DevTools, stack traces, and search results point to the wrong component during auth debugging

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
Object-URL state, Blob and revokeObjectURL bookkeeping can be replaced with a data: URL. The latest object URL is never revoked on close or unmount
Backup codes are stored as decryptable ciphertext using symmetricEncrypt instead of one-way hashes, making them recoverable if DB and app key material are exposed
Store backup codes as one-way hashes instead of a reversible encrypted blob
req.body.backupCode.replaceAll() runs on unvalidated body - a truthy non-string backupCode (number, array, object) throws TypeError returning unhandled 500 instead of 400

BackupCode.tsx line 7 exports function TwoFactor instead of function BackupCode - wrong function name will appear in React DevTools and error stack traces causing confusion since a real TwoFactor component already exists

`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw (or return a non-array) if `backupCodes` is corrupted/unexpected, which would crash the authorize/disable flow with a 500. Consider guarding parse/decrypt errors and validating the decoded shape before using `indexOf`
Test suite doesn't cover login-with-backup-code, disable-via-backup-code, or sequential reuse failure, so the recovery path can regress without CI noticing
The backup-code verification block (key guard, missing-codes guard, decrypt and JSON.parse, strip '-', indexOf) is duplicated in disable.ts:48-64

Backup code validation reads full plaintext list, checks in memory, then writes back updated encrypted array - this leaves backup codes recoverable at rest and opens a TOCTOU window where two parallel requests can both pass the lookup before either write null
Nothing tests backup-code login, single-use rejection on reuse, a wrong code, missing codes, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. The new test only clicks Download, Copy and Close
user.twoFactorEnabled && (line 48) and else if (user.twoFactorEnabled) (line 69) are always true after the early return at line 36, and the CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY check is copied into both branches
req.body.backupCode.replaceAll is called on an unvalidated body, so a truthy non-string backupCode throws a TypeError and returns 500 instead of 400

Component is exported as `function TwoFactor` even though it's a backup-code UI; the name mismatch can be confusing in stack traces/DevTools and when importing alongside the real `TwoFactor` component
The component in BackupCode.tsx is exported as function TwoFactor (copy-paste), so DevTools and stack traces show two different components as TwoFactor

Renders an `<a>` wrapping a `Button` that becomes a `<button>`, which creates nested interactive elements (`<a><button>…`). This can cause inconsistent click/keyboard behavior and is invalid HTML semantics

No tests exist for backup-code auth paths: login with backup code, rejection of used code, wrong code, missing-codes case, and disabling 2FA with backup code - only Download, Copy and Close buttons are tested

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
Blob URL for backup code download is not revoked when modal is closed/reset - only revoked when generating a new URL, causing memory leaks for the page session lifetime
Password visibility toggle button has tabIndex={-1} which removes it from keyboard navigation, causing accessibility regression for keyboard-only users

locator.isChecked() returns a Promise<boolean>, so expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() only asserts that a Promise object exists, not its resolved value - should use data-state attribute check instead

Backup code reuse vulnerability via TOCTOU race condition - the non-atomic read-check-write pattern allows two concurrent login requests with the same backup code to both pass validation before either marks the code as used

A new object URL is created for `backupCodesUrl`, but it's only revoked when generating a new one; if the modal is closed/reset without another setup run, the object URL can leak and keep the blob alive longer than intended

Dismissing the dialog (via Escape key or clicking outside) during the backup codes step bypasses the onEnable callback, causing the UI to show 2FA as disabled even though it was successfully enabled on the server because utils.viewer.me.invalidate() is never called

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Clipboard copy operation not properly handled - navigator.clipboard.writeText() is called without awaiting or catching failures, but immediately shows a success toast even if clipboard write is blocked/denied
When totpEmail is present the login page switches to ExternalTotpFooter, so SAML/Google users never see the new backup-code entry point and can still be locked out after losing their authenticator
Migration timestamp 20230804153419 is older than existing migrations like 20230828094603, causing Prisma migration-order drift across environments
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login
The new else-if branches for IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes duplicate the existing errorMessages map whose fallback already covers these codes

navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited, so the 'copied' toast shows even when the write fails. On plain-HTTP non-localhost self-hosted installs navigator.clipboard is undefined and the click throws

onEnable (viewer.me.invalidate) now runs only from the backup-codes Close button. Dismissing with Esc, overlay click or X leaves 2FA enabled in DB but shown as off, and reopening shows stale DisplayBackupCodes step because resetState never runs

The backup-code comparison is case- and whitespace-sensitive (only '-' is stripped). Codes are lowercase hex but input does not turn off auto-capitalize, so valid codes are rejected on iOS. Same issue in disable.ts:61 and BackupCode.tsx

Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have backupCodes = NULL and are told to 'generate them in your settings', but no regenerate UI or endpoint exists. Once all codes are used, the array is all nulls and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes

A valid backup code plus any non-empty totpCode authenticates without the password: the password check at ~:121 runs only when !credentials.totpCode, and the new backup-code branch never verifies totpCode

After enabling 2FA, onEnable() and utils.viewer.me.invalidate() only runs from backup-codes Close button; dismissing with Esc, overlay click, or X button only toggles open state, causing settings switch and badge to show 2FA disabled while it's enabled in DB, and resetState never runs so reopening shows stale DisplayBackupCodes step
tabIndex={-1} on the shared PasswordField show/hide button takes it out of the tab order for every password field in the app
The patch switched to PasswordField but kept type="password". PasswordField spreads {...props} after its own computed type, so the show-password toggle never reveals the value

First e2e test assertion on line 53 uses expect(Promise).toBeTruthy() which evaluates the Promise object itself (always truthy) rather than the resolved boolean - should use await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()
The patch adds a FIXME noting that expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() always passes (a Promise is truthy), but leaves the assertion unfixed

First e2e test never interacts with the new backup codes screen after OTP verification - it skips straight to checking the two-factor-switch without clicking backup-codes-close, so onEnable() is never called
The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.

Backup-code consumption is read-decrypt-null-write with no transaction or compare-and-swap, so concurrent logins can reuse one code, and last-write-wins can bring back a code another login already consumed
The Download control is a Button nested inside an anchor, which is invalid interactive-content nesting

PasswordField on line 167 has explicit type="password" prop that breaks the show/hide password toggle because {...props} spread in InputField comes after the internal type prop, causing the explicit type to always override the dynamic isPasswordVisible state
The new branch throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) when the encryption key is missing, instead of returning res.status(500).json like the rest of the file
A redundant fragment wraps a single div

Backup code authentication skips password verification - when credentials.totpCode is non-empty, password verification is bypassed, allowing an attacker to authenticate with only a valid backup code by sending any non-empty totpCode

Backup-code consumption is non-atomic (read, decrypt, null-slot, write-back) with no transaction or compare-and-swap, allowing concurrent logins with the same code to all succeed and last-write-wins can restore a consumed code
`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` isn't awaited/handled, so the success toast can show even if the clipboard write fails (e.g., permissions/unsupported environment)

Password verification can be bypassed when a crafted request includes both a valid backupCode and any truthy totpCode value. The password check on line 121 is skipped when totpCode is present, but the backup code branch still runs and grants authentication. An attacker with a stolen backup code can log in without knowing the password.
const mockUser: User lacks the new required backupCodes field. The type-check script does not include this file so CI will not flag it

SSO users still can't authenticate with backup codes because guards only exempt totpCode - a Google/SAML user submitting backupCode will hit ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled or IncorrectEmailPassword before the backup-code branch runs

issues.claim: Backup code comparison uses indexOf, which is case-sensitive, and only '-' is stripped from the input. Valid codes typed in a different case or with whitespace are rejected, for example uppercase from iOS auto-capitalize. The same comparison appears in disable.ts and BackupCode.tsx.

Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read, decrypt, check, null-slot and write-back, with no transaction, lock or compare-and-swap. Concurrent requests can both accept the same backup code, and last-write-wins can restore a code that was already consumed.
Backup codes are stored as reversible ciphertext via symmetricEncrypt instead of one-way hashes, so they can be recovered if the DB and the app key are exposed.
The component exported from BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` instead of `BackupCode`. It collides with the existing TwoFactor component in DevTools, stack traces and imports.
The object URL created for the backup-codes download is only revoked when a new one is generated. It is never revoked when the modal is closed, reset or unmounted, so the blob leaks.
`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll()` is called on an unvalidated body. A truthy non-string backupCode throws a TypeError and returns 500 instead of 400.
`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on backupCodes is unguarded. Corrupted data can throw or return a non-array, which crashes the authorize/disable flow with a 500.
No tests cover login with a backup code, rejection of a reused or wrong code, the missing-codes case, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. The new test only exercises Download, Copy and Close.
The backup-code verification block (key guard, missing-codes guard, decrypt and JSON.parse, strip '-', indexOf) is duplicated in disable.ts:48-64.

The `user.twoFactorEnabled &&` check (line 48) and the `else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)` check (line 69) are always true after the early return at line 36. The CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY check is copied into both branches.
The Download control renders a Button (a `<button>`) nested inside an `<a>`, which is invalid nested interactive content.
The shared PasswordField show/hide toggle button has tabIndex={-1}, which removes it from keyboard tab order for every password field.
The e2e assertion `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks a Promise object, which is always truthy, rather than the resolved boolean. It is left unfixed despite an added FIXME.

onEnable (`utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`) runs only from the backup-codes Close button. Dismissing the dialog via Escape, overlay click or X leaves 2FA enabled in the DB but shown as disabled. Because resetState never runs, reopening shows the stale DisplayBackupCodes step.

`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` is not awaited or error-handled, so the success toast shows even when the write fails. Where navigator.clipboard is undefined (plain-HTTP non-localhost), the click throws.
When totpEmail is present, the login page renders ExternalTotpFooter, so SAML/Google users never see the backup-code entry point.
The authorize guards exempt only totpCode. An SSO (Google/SAML) user submitting a backupCode hits ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled or IncorrectEmailPassword before the backup-code branch runs.
Migration timestamp 20230804153419 is older than existing migrations such as 20230828094603, which causes Prisma migration-order drift.
An error message in the disable endpoint refers to 'backup code login'.
The new else-if branches for IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes duplicate the existing errorMessages map, whose fallback already covers these codes.

Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have backupCodes = NULL and are told to generate them in settings, but no regenerate UI or endpoint exists. Once all codes are used, the array is all nulls and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes.

The password check (~line 121) runs only when totpCode is falsy, and the backup-code branch never verifies totpCode. A valid backupCode plus any non-empty totpCode therefore authenticates without the password.
PasswordField (line 167) is passed an explicit type="password". Because {...props} is spread after the computed type, the show/hide toggle never reveals the value.
The first e2e test never clicks backup-codes-close after OTP verification, so onEnable() is never called before the two-factor-switch is checked.
The new branch throws `new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when the encryption key is missing, instead of returning `res.status(500).json` like the rest of the file.
A redundant fragment wraps a single div.
`const mockUser: User` lacks the new required backupCodes field, and the type-check script does not include this file.
